The statute described is Section 274A of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA), specifically the employer sanctions provision. Its primary legal implication is that it imposes civil and criminal liability on employers who knowingly hire, recruit, or refer for a fee individuals who are not authorized to work in the United States. To comply with this law, employers are required to verify the identity and employment authorization of every employee hired after November 6, 1986, by completing Form I-9. Failure to adhere to these verification requirements or knowingly hiring unauthorized workers can result in substantial monetary fines, which vary based on the number of violations and whether they are considered repeat offenses. In severe cases involving patterns of practice, criminal penalties, including imprisonment, may also apply.
